violations.message: Domain file src/delivery/__models__/deliveryman.model.ts imports forbidden package typeorm
Domain file src/delivery/__models__/orders.model.ts imports forbidden package typeorm

updateDeliverymansInfo sets firstName and lastName directly on the Deliveryman aggregate. The other services in this module change it only through model methods (addOrder, changeStatus, addNewMessageToOrders). Its `!== undefined ??` guard also means the assignment never runs.

UpdateOrderService is an Orders use case: it injects OrdersRepository from src/delivery/orders/dal, uses UpdateOrderDto from src/delivery/orders/dtos and returns Order. It belongs in the orders module, not in the deliveryman services module.

The domain class Deliveryman holds persistence mapping, which belongs in the infrastructure layer: @Entity('deliverymans') sets the table name, @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') and @Column({ default: false }) set key generation and column defaults, and @OneToMany with cascade ['insert','update'] sets ORM write cascading. Moving this mapping into an infrastructure persistence model or schema would leave the domain entity free of persistence concerns.

Domain class Order defines how it is stored in the database using TypeORM decorators: @Entity('orders'), @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid'), @Column({ default: true }), and @ManyToOne/@JoinColumn on deliverymanId. Table, column, default and foreign-key mapping is a persistence (infrastructure) responsibility that does not belong in the domain layer.
